content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"Understanding is God-given spiritual discernment: the divinely granted capacity to perceive, comprehend, and rightly apply God's truth, will, and moral order. It is inseparable from wisdom and rooted in the fear of the Lord, encompassing illumination of Scripture, insight into divine mysteries, and (as listed alternatives) moral discernment, practical skill, and prophetic insight.","book_summary":"Understanding is specifically the discernment of good from evil, and it is gained through the moral act of departing from evil and doing God's commandments ('a good understanding have all they that do his commandments').","consensus_core_identification":"God-given spiritual discernment/comprehension of divine truth broadly — illumination enabling one to grasp and apply God's word, will, and moral order.","book_core_identification":"Moral discernment of good from evil, acquired conditionally through obedience — departing from evil and keeping God's commandments.","core_relation":"BOOK_NARROWS","extension_relation":"BOOK_SUBSET","boundary_disagreement":"The book restricts understanding to ethical discernment (good vs. evil) obtained through obedient practice, excluding or at least omitting the broader consensus cases: intellectual/spiritual comprehension of divine mysteries, scriptural illumination (Luke 24:45; Eph 1:17-18), prophetic decoding (Daniel), and Spirit-given craftsmanship. It also adds a conditional mechanism — understanding is gained BY departing from evil and doing commandments — whereas the consensus treats it primarily as a granted gift or faculty, with obedience as fruit rather than acquisition-condition.","material_contradiction":"","rationale":"The book stays within the consensus's general category (understanding as a God-oriented discernment tied to the fear of the Lord) — indeed Response A cites Job 28:28 in its primary basis, and Response C lists moral discernment of good and evil as a common alternative. However, the book materially tightens the definition to only the moral-practical dimension and reframes understanding as something earned through obedience rather than granted illumination. This changes the boundary and conditions without replacing the central referent, fitting REFINED rather than MATCH (the cores are not equivalent in scope) and not DIVERGENT (no contradiction of the consensus referent).","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"One could argue MATCH: the book's definition is a direct quotation-level paraphrase of Job 28:28 and Ps 111:10, both of which appear in the consensus's own primary basis, so the book may simply be foregrounding one strand of an already-shared meaning rather than genuinely excluding the others. Since the entry never explicitly denies the broader illumination sense, the narrowing might be emphasis rather than boundary disagreement.","confidence":"medium"}
